newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK investors wary of China/Taiwan shipping ties.
newsitem.headline: HK investors wary of China/Taiwan shipping ties.

text.p: Hong Kong stock investors greeted the prospects of direct shipping links between Taiwan and China with caution on Thursday, although most brokers said the long-term effect to the territory was likely to be small.
The Hang Seng Index was down 75.59 points or 0.55 percent at 13,617.20 at the midday break, partly on worries that direct shipping links across the Taiwan Strait could divert business from Hong Kong.
"People realise that it is not just the physical trade but all the income that goes to the middlemen that we are going to lose," said Janet Gillies, sales director at OCBC Securities.

On Wednesday, non-government negotiators from Taiwan and China reached an understanding to allow shipping companies to seek approval from China to sail between Kaohsiung in Taiwan and Fuzhou and Xiamen in China's Fujian province.
Most trade between Taiwan and China now passes through third countries, usually Hong Kong, due to Taipei's decades-old ban on direct links with the mainland.
But many brokers said the actual diversion of flows away from Hong Kong was likely to be minimal.

"We (Hong Kong) are likely to lose only about five percent of our total trade," said James Robertson, vice president of Salomon Brothers. "But this has been developing for some time now and most people have factored it into their equations."
The prospect should be viewed as more as a long-term economic or business development, said Adrian Ngan, director of Peregrine Securities.
"It (the understanding) will not have much of an impact in the near term," Ngan said.
Ngan noted the understanding between the two long-time rivals was not entirely based on economics and warned that it could all change overnight.
While the overall Hong Kong market had been dampened, brokers said it was hard to point to individual issues that would be hurt by direct cross-strait shipping links.

Glenn Lesko, head of equities trading at HG Asia, noted that many economically and politically sensitive stocks such as Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, Swire Pacific Ltd and Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd were little changed.
He said that showed the development was not a short-term issue, although it merited long-term attention.
Conglomerate and port operator Hutchison was unchanged at HK$64.25, Swire was up HK$0.25 at HK$75.00 and Cathay was up HK$0.05 at HK$11.95.
One analyst at a U.S. brokerage said the developments are likely to have the greatest positive impact on Xiamen, which has a very good deep water port.
"The government has wanted to develop that zone for a long time," he added. "In the longer term, this could benefit Hong Kong as the hub of greater China."

Min Xin Holdings Ltd rose HK$0.15 to HK$3.125 on anticipation it would benefit from economic growth in Fujian. The Fujian-based company is engaged in infrastructural and property development, finance, banking and insurance.
